spec.name: Cyanotype Spitfire Mk I
spec.description: A low-poly Supermarine Spitfire rendered as a living cyanotype blueprint: deep Prussian-blue panels traced with glowing cyan seam lines, paper-white roundels, rivets and hand-inked annotations, standing nose-up on its taildragger undercarriage.
spec.layout: A Spitfire facing +Z, nose at z≈+4.9, tail at z≈−5.0, resting on three wheels: the two main wheels (radius 0.35, hubs at y=0.35, x≈±2.05, z≈0.75) touch y=0, and the small tailwheel at z≈−4.2 keeps the fuselage level with a slight nose-up stance. The elliptical monocoque fuselage runs from the engine cowl (z 4.3) tapering back through the cockpit (z≈0.3) to a slim tail cone ending at z=−3.6; belly line y≈1.15, spine y≈2.5. The wing is one low-mounted elliptical plate spanning x −5.6..+5.6 at y 1.25..1.75, meeting the fuselage belly at mount wingRoot, with a rounded tip, a dihedral-free flat top, a radiator bath under the port wing and gun fairings forward of the outer panels; ailerons hinge at the trailing edge from x≈2.8 outward. The empennage fills z −5.3..−3.4: a broad elliptical tailplane with hinged elevators and a tall rounded fin to y=3.4 with a hinged rudder reaching back to z≈−5.0, plus a tailskid above the tailwheel. The nose and canopy part owns the pale-steel spinner cone at mount spinnerBase with five propeller blades on joint propHub, and the framed bubble canopy rising from mount canopyBase to y≈2.95. Style everywhere: every panel is a flat cyanotype blue; seams, rivets, panel edges, hatch outlines, registration letters, serials, roundel rings and little inked callout arrows are separate thin parts in glowing cyan and paper white laid on the blue; spinner, hubs, gunsight and pitot are pale steel-blue; cockpit glazing is pale cyan; the only warm note is a tiny amber beacon on the fin tip.

parts.builds: The whole monocoque hull except nose spinner and canopy: build the body as a smooth low-poly loft/sweep along z from the firewall (z=4.3, roughly 1.1 wide × 0.95 tall ellipse at y≈1.9) swelling through the cockpit bay (z≈0.3, widest ~1.05 half-width, belly y≈1.15, spine y≈2.5) and tapering to the tail cone at mount tailRoot (z=−3.6, about 0.32 half-width, centred y≈1.85). Sections read as faceted ellipse sweeps (circle sections with modest sides, or loft stations). Wear hullBlue with panelBlue sectors on the upper spine and cowlBlue on the forward engine cowl ring. Details as seated thin parts: a ring of cyan panel-seam lines around the cowl (3 hoops of thin rods), exhaust stubs (six small dark angled frustum boxes, 3 per side at z 3.3..2.6 along the flank, deepInk with steelPale rims), paper-white rivet dots scattered in neat rows along two spine seams and around each panel line, a white serial text block on the rear flank ('P7350 AR·F' style, built from tiny inkWhite quads or extrude strokes), a small inked callout arrow (thin lineCyan stick with a chevron head) pointing at the fuel hatch on the starboard flank, an oil-stain patch (thin oilStain plate) low on the belly under the cowl, and the aft fuselage/wing fairing fillet reaching down to mount wingRoot. Also build the belly pitot-less fairing strip. Rides joint airframe.
parts.attaches: Nose face at mount spinnerBase hands over to the nose & canopy part; rear end at mount tailRoot hands over to empennage; underside fairing meets the wings at mount wingRoot; all rides joint airframe.

parts.builds: Both wings as one low elliptical plate: span x −5.6..+5.6, chord from z≈−0.6 (trailing edge) to z≈2.0 (leading edge), thickness y 1.28..1.72 with a rounded leading edge and knife trailing edge, meeting the fuselage belly at mount wingRoot. Wing tops wear hullBlue with panelBlue outer panels; the underside reads darker radiDark. Signature cyanotype details: a full set of paper-white national roundels on both upper wings (inner ring disc steelHub, outer ring lineCyan, built as thin stacked discs seated on the surface, radius ~0.55 at x≈±3.6, z≈1.0) and small inkWhite fin-flash rectangles are NOT here (they belong to empennage); gun fairings: two shallow blister boxes per wing forward of z≈1.4 at x≈±2.2 and ±2.9 in hullBlue with inkWhite rivet rows; the radiator bath: a recessed under-wing scoop at x≈−1.0, z≈0.9 with a slatted grid of thin steelPale bars; a paper-white wingtip light plate at each tip (x≈±5.5); ailerons: hinged trailing-edge flaps from x 2.8 to 5.2 on each side, thin wedge slabs hanging on joints aileronL/aileronR, hullBlue with a lineCyan hinge line and small white trim-tab marks; cyan panel-seam hoops crossing the wing chord at z≈1.6, 0.6 and −0.2 on both sides; an inkCyan annotation arrow near the port aileron; and a tiny pitot tube (thin steelPale rod) under the starboard wingtip leading edge. Wing geometry rides airframe; the ailerons ride aileronL/aileronR.
parts.attaches: Root chord sits on the fuselage fairing at mount wingRoot; the undercarriage legs hang from mounts gearAnchorL and gearAnchorR built by the undercarriage part; ailerons hinge on joints aileronL/aileronR.

parts.builds: The tail: from mount tailRoot (z=−3.6) build a slim tail cone continuation for the first 0.3 m, then the empennage. Tailplane: a flat elliptical plate spanning x −2.1..+2.1, chord z −4.9..−3.6, at y≈1.9, hullBlue on top with paper-white roundel-less plain panels, cyan seam line across each side at z≈−4.2, and hinged elevator wedges (the outer chord from z −4.9..−4.2 on each half) on joints elevatorL/elevatorR with lineCyan hinge lines and a white trim tab mark on the port elevator. Fin: a tall rounded dorsal blade rising from the spine (y≈2.1 at z=−3.6) sweeping back and up to y=3.4, reaching back to z≈−4.6, hullBlue forward face with a panelBlue leading-edge strip; its rudder (from z≈−4.35 aft, on joint rudder) wears the same hullBlue with three thin horizontal lineCyan hinge lines, a white rudder trim tab at its lower corner, and the classic paper-white fin flash: three vertical stripe plates (steelHub / roddGreen / steelHub, each ~0.12 wide) near the fin's leading edge. Rudder geometry rides joint rudder; fin and tailplane ride airframe. Add a small tailskid: a short angled steelPale rod above the tailwheel position (z≈−4.1, down to y≈0.45), a tiny amber beacon dome (beacon, small lathe dome with a lineCyan rim) on the fin tip, and an inked lineCyan arrow pointing at the tailplane adjuster on the underside.
parts.attaches: Forward faces meet the fuselage cone at mount tailRoot; elevators hinge on elevatorL/elevatorR, rudder on rudder; the tailwheel fork top is shared with the undercarriage part at [0, 0.55, -4.1].

parts.builds: The taildragger running gear, the only part touching the floor. Two main legs: from mounts gearAnchorL/gearAnchorR (x≈±0.62 on the wing underside) angled raked-forward-and-outward steelPale frustum rods down to wheel hubs at [±2.05, 0.35, 0.75] (on joints wheelFL/wheelFR); each leg gets a small V-brace (thin steelPale rod back to the wing underside near x≈±1.1, z≈0.4) and a hinged retract cover plate (thin hullBlue slab with a lineCyan edge) between the legs. Wheels: flat-cylindrical tyres (tyre, radius 0.35, width 0.16, low-poly with 12 flat side facets) with a steelHub hub disc, five lineCyan spoke studs, a deepInk tread ring seated on the rim, and a tiny inkWhite serial dot. Both wheels ride wheelFL/wheelFR. Tailwheel: a smaller wheel (radius 0.14) at [0, 0.32, −4.2] on joint tailwheel in a short steelPale fork that reaches up to [0, 0.55, −4.1] to meet the empennage tailskid, same hub treatment scaled down. Add small dust-grey mud marks (oilStain thin patches) low on the leg roots and a tiny inkCyan annotation arrow by the starboard leg.
parts.attaches: Leg roots bolt to the wing underside at mounts gearAnchorL/gearAnchorR; hubs on joints wheelFL/wheelFR and tailwheel; tail fork top meets the empennage tailskid.

parts.builds: The nose and cockpit furniture. Spinner: a pale-steel (steelPale) lathe cone from mount spinnerBase (z=4.3, base radius 0.42) tapering to a rounded tip at z≈4.9, with three lineCyan spin-ring hoops and a small inkWhite crest dot at the tip; ride it on airframe. Propeller: five blades on joint propHub — each a tapered flat wooden blade (roddGreen, ~1.55 long, widest ~0.17 near the root) with a paper-white tip band (~0.2 at the outer end), a steelPale root cuff cylinder, and an inkWhite rivet line; blades fan evenly around the hub. Cockpit: from mount canopyBase build the windscreen and sliding bubble canopy as a low-poly framed glazing — a shallow glass dome (glazing, faceted sphere segment) from y≈2.42 to y≈2.95 over z 0.35..−0.75, carried on a light steelPale frame of thin hoops and rails with inkWhite rivets, plus a fixed 3-panel windscreen wedge at z≈0.55 tilting back. Inside and behind: a steelPale pilot seat back plate, a deepInk headrest block under the spine fairing, a tiny gunsight (steelPale post with an inkWhite ring) on the coaming, and a small lineCyan instrument glow quad on the dash face. Add two tiny inkWhite wiper/annotation ticks beside the canopy rail. Rides airframe; the propeller blades ride propHub.
parts.attaches: Spinner base sits on the fuselage nose face at mount spinnerBase; canopy base sits on the fuselage spine at mount canopyBase; blades on joint propHub.

calls.reasoning:
Here's a thinking process that leads to the suggested JSON spec:

1.  **Analyze the Request & Constraints:**
    *   **Goal:** Create a single JSON specification that describes a Spitfire fighter plane model.
    *   **Context:** TheI need to write a spec JSON for a Spitfire fighter plane in cyanotype blueprint style. Style: cyanotype blueprint — deep blue background isn't allowed (only the model). The model itself should look like a blueprint drawing: deep cyan-blue body, white/pale-cyan "ink" lines, glowing cyan edges? Actually a cyanotype blueprint style model: the plane rendered in blueprint cyan tones — deep Prussian blue surfaces with lighter cyan linework, white annotations. Since every surface is a flat colour, "linework" means small parts in their own colours: panel seams, rivets, roundels, registration numbers, drawn as thin plates/sticks in pale cyan/white.

Plan the plane: a Spitfire. Size roughly: wingspan ~9m? Spitfire wingspan 11.2m, length 9.1m, height ~3.5m. But stylized model — keep real-world size: length ~9.2m along Z (front +Z), wingspan ~11m along X, height ~3m on tailfin? Wait, front faces +Z, so length along Z. The model faces +Z: nose at +Z. Standing on its landing gear (taildragger): wheels at front (under wing), tail skid at back. So fuselage tilted slightly? Spitfire sits nose-high slightly on tailwheel. Keep simple: level fuselage at height ~1.9m (top of fuselage), belly ~1.5m, wheels radius ~0.3m touching floor.

Size: width 11.2 (wingspan), height ~3.4 (tail fin top), length 9.5.

Coordinate: nose at z=+4.7, tail at z=-4.8.

Parts (3-6): 
1. fuselage (monocoque, spinner, cockpit frame) 
2. wing assembly (wings, ailerons, roundels, landing gear legs + wheels? gear could be own part)
3. empennage (tailplane, fin, rudder, tailskid)
4. landing gear (undercarriage legs, wheels, tailwheel)
5. cockpit canopy & details (canopy, pilot seat, exhaust stubs, guns)?

Give 5 parts. Budgets sum ≤900. Say 4 parts with ~200 each or 5 parts ~170 each.

Joints: could be static (joints: []). A Spitfire display — propeller could spin (hinge joints for prop, wheels, rudder, ailerons). Rigging nice: prop hub joint, wheelFL/wheelFR, tailwheel, rudder joint, elevator joints, ailerons. Keep moderate: propeller, rudder, elevatorL/elevatorR, aileronL/aileronR, wheels. That's 8-9 joints. Order parents first, root first.

Root joint: "airframe" at [0, 1.9, 0] dir [0,1,0] role spine.

Joints:
- airframe root
- propHub parent airframe at [0,1.9,4.55] dir [0,0,1] role hinge, group propeller
- rudder parent airframe at [0,2.2,-4.5] dir [0,1,0]? Rudder hinges about vertical axis — dir is bone direction; use dir [0,0,-1] maybe. Role hinge.
- elevators: dir [1,0,0]/[-1,0,0] hinge at tailplane tips.
- ailerons at outer wings.
- wheelFL/wheelFR dir [1,0,0]/[-1,0,0] role hinge at hub centres, height 0.3.
- tailwheel.

Mounts:
- wingCenter [0, 1.45, 0.6] where wings meet fuselage belly
- gearRoots? Mounts where parts meet: fuselage-wing junction, fuselage-tail junction (rear fuselage taper), canopy base, prop spinner base, gear attach points.

Mounts list:
- wingBoxFront/rear? Simpler: "wingRoot" [0, 1.45, 0.55] fuselage underside where the wing fairing sits.
- tailRoot [0, 1.75, -3.6] rear fuselage end where empennage attaches.
- spinnerBase [0, 1.9, 4.3] nose.
- canopyBase [0, 2.3, 0.3] top of fuselage at cockpit.
- gearAnchorL [0.55, 1.4, 0.7], gearAnchorR [-0.55, 1.4, 0.7] where undercarriage legs meet wing underside.
- propShaft included in spinnerBase.

Palette (≤24): cyanotype blues: 
- "blueDeep": "#0a2a4a" (dark Prussian blue hull)
- "blueMid": "#123c66" (panel blue)
- "blueLight": "#2a6fa8"
- "cyanLine": "#4fd8ff" (glowing linework/annotations)
- "paper": "#dceeff" (white-blue ink highlights, roundels)
- "ink": "#0e1626" (dark lines, cockpit)
- "dullMetal": "#8fb7d9" (spinner/pale steel)
- "accent": "#ffb347"? Blueprint usually monochrome; but a red accent? Cyanotype style typically all blues + white. Maybe keep monochrome plus a faint warm accent for warning marks — keep pure cyanotype: use whites and cyans only, maybe one amber for a beacon light. I'll include "beacon": "#ff6a3c" tiny light. Also "tread" dark, "canopyTint": translucent-ish flat "#7fd4ff", "tyre": "#14202e", "hub": "#c9e6ff", "oil": "#16324f".

Parts:
1. "fuselage": 175 budget. Elliptical monocoque from spinner to tail cone: sweep/loft along z from z=4.3 to z=-3.6, engine cowl panels, exhaust stubs, panel seams as thin cyan sticks/lines, cockpit opening (canopy built by another part? canopy assigned to fuselage or own part). Give canopy to fuselage? Make part 5 "canopy & cockpit"? Let's define 5 parts:

1. fuselage (hull, nose cowl, exhaust stubs, panel lines) — box [[-0.85,0.9,-3.6],[0.85,2.5,4.55]]
2. wings (both wings, ailerons with joints, roundels, wingtip lights, gun fairings under wing, wing fuel tank? Radiator under starboard wing) — box [[-5.6,1.25,-0.9],[5.6,1.75,2.0]]
3. empennage (tailplane both sides, fin, rudder, elevators, tailskid, flash on fin?) — box [[-2.1,1.4,-5.3],[2.1,3.4,-3.4]]
4. undercarriage (both main legs, wheels, spats?, tailwheel, radiator bath under port wing? radiator is wing detail—assign to wings) — box [[-1.6,0,-1.0],[1.6,1.45,1.3]]
5. cockpit & propeller (spinner, prop blades on propHub, canopy glazing frames, pilot seat, instruments)? Hmm propeller belongs at nose — that's in fuselage box. Maybe part 5 = "nose & canopy": spinner, prop blades, canopy, headrest, exhaust? But fuselage already owns cowl. Split: fuselage owns bare hull+cowl; part 5 owns spinner, propeller blades, canopy, pilot seat, guns on top? Guns on Spitfire were in wings. 

Parts split evenly: 
1. fuselage: hull from nose ring to tail cone, engine cowl, exhaust stubs, panel seams, wing fairing. budget 190
2. wings: both wings + ailerons + roundels + gun fairings + pitot + radiator bath. budget 200
3. empennage: tailplane, fin, rudder, elevators, tailskid. budget 160
4. undercarriage: legs, wheels, hubs, tailwheel, retract covers. budget 150
5. nose & canopy: spinner, propeller blades (on propHub), canopy frames + glazing, seat, headrest, gunsight. budget 200

Total 900. Good.

Boxes:
- fuselage: [[-0.9, 0.85, -3.6], [0.9, 2.5, 4.3]] (nose up to 4.3 where spinner takes over; spinner extends to ~4.75, prop to ~5.3? Then size length larger. Prop radius ~1.7m blades — prop disc at z≈4.5, blades extend to 4.9 z. Width of model dominated by wings 11.2. Length: tail -5.0 to prop tip 5.0 ≈ 10? Hmm spinners: spinner from 4.3 to 4.9, blades span vertically 1.9±1.7... blades on hub at z=4.55, length 1.6, so blade tips z≈4.6 (they're mostly radial in x-y plane). So prop doesn't extend z beyond spinner much. Length z: -5.2 (rudder tail) to +4.9 (spinner tip) ≈ 10.1. Height: tailfin top ~3.4. So size [11.2, 3.4, 10.2]. Hmm that's big but fine — real Spitfire.

Actually with wing span 11.2 and landing gear under wings at x≈±2.0, wheels at z≈0.6. Floor contact: wheels bottom y=0. Wheel radius 0.35, hub at y=0.35.

Fuselage: belly at y≈1.15 (undercockpit), top at y≈2.5 (spine forward), tapering tail to y≈1.7 at z=-3.6. Wing at y 1.3–1.75.

Let me write mounts:
- "wingRoot": [0, 1.5, 0.6]
- "tailRoot": [0, 1.85, -3.6]
- "spinnerBase": [0, 1.9, 4.3]
- "canopyBase": [0, 2.42, 0.35]
- "gearAnchorL": [0.62, 1.3, 0.75], "gearAnchorR": [-0.62, 1.3, 0.75]

Joints: static? Rigging adds value (prop spin, wheel roll, rudder). Include:

- airframe: root, at [0,1.8,0], dir [0,1,0], role spine
- propHub: parent airframe, at [0,1.9,4.55], dir [0,0,1], role hinge, group propeller
- rudder: parent airframe, at [0,2.4,-4.4], dir [0,0,-1], role hinge, group tail
- elevatorL: parent airframe at [1.3,2.0,-4.6] dir [1,0,0] hinge group tail
- elevatorR: [-1.3,...] dir [-1,0,0]
- aileronL: parent airframe at [4.2,1.5,-0.5] dir [1,0,0] hinge group wings — aileron chord line at trailing edge x≈4.2.
- aileronR mirror.
- wheelFL: at [2.05,0.35,0.75] dir [1,0,0] hinge group undercarriage
- wheelFR: [-2.05,...] dir [-1,0,0]
- tailwheel: at [0,0.35,-4.2] dir [0,1,0]? wheels spin about axle x; tailwheel dir [1,0,0].

Each part lists joints its geometry rides: geometry rides nearest joint by default; list the ones they attach to.

Wings attach via wingRoot mount, ride airframe. Fuselage rides airframe. Empennage rides airframe + rudder/elevators. Undercarriage rides airframe + wheelFL/wheelFR. Nose&canopy rides airframe + propHub.

Layout text: describe silhouette, front to back, floor rest, style.

Style description: every surface wears deep Prussian-blue cel blues; panel seams, rivets, roundels, registration letters, hatches and annotations are separate thin parts in glowing cyan and paper-white "ink"; the spinner, hubs and pitot read as pale steel; cockpit glazing pale cyan; small beacon light amber for one warm accent.

Write the JSON. Keep descriptions detailed but concise-ish. Budget sums: 190+200+160+150+200=900.
